messages:
opsbot: Pagerduty alert -> Incident INC-2026-03-17: Suspicious egress from staging logshipper to external domain analytics.example.net. Elevated P1 and paging on-call (vikram). bridge: https://meet/incident/8401239876

vikram: on it, joining bridge. runbook?

opsbot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-leak. bridge created.

jordan: quick triage: staging logshipper started POSTing gzipped batches to analytics.example.net since ~02:12 UTC. Found Authorization headers in log payloads (looks like service tokens). Sample snippet below (scrubbed):

```
2026-03-17T02:14:10Z INFO forwarder POST https://analytics.example.net/upload size=4.2MB headers={"authorization":"Bearer sk-live-XXXX...","x-request-id":"req_abc123"} path=/var/log/proxy/access.log.2026-03-17.gz
```

jordan: contains truncated bearer tokens and internal request ids. likely svc-infer-shipper creds ended up in raw logs.

sara: confirming host tags -> staging-logs-5. not prod (good). tokens appear to be service creds, rotated monthly.

neal: proposed mitigations: 1) stop logshipper service on staging, 2) firewall egress block to analytics.example.net, 3) rotate svc-infer-shipper keys, 4) scan S3 for uploaded objects.

vikram: executing 1 & 2 now. will confirm when done. sara — can you take key rotation and coordinate with CI deploy?

sara: starting rotation for svc-infer-shipper. creating new keys and pushing to staging config. ETA ~8m. also opening PR to add header redaction before upload. PR: https://git/internal/pr/5421

jordan: I copied suspect objects for analysis: s3://staging-logs/shipper/2026-03-17/*.gz -> downloaded locally for forensics. No customer PII seen in cursory scan; primary sensitive material are Authorization headers and internal IDs. uploading manifest+md5 to redwood-secure-evidence.

opsbot: Reminder: evidence uploads must target redwood-secure-evidence and use KMS key KMS-CRYPTO-1; retention 90d.

vikram: egress block applied by firewall team — analytics.example.net unreachable from staging subnets. logshipper process stopped on 3 hosts. sara, status on key rotation?

sara: new key pair created and deployed to staging config; old keys revoked. updated secrets in vault and rotated. routing updated, CI rollout completed. added redaction middleware to log pipeline to strip Authorization header. PR merged and deployed to staging: ci/deploy/sha-abcde.

neal: running network scan for any other third-party endpoints. initial run: 4 uploads total to analytics.example.net between 02:12-02:17 UTC, all from staging. no prod hits. collecting flow logs and correlation ids now. will post full CSV to secure evidence bucket.

jordan: I've pinged @product-security with summary. product-security: please advise on customer notification threshold. current verdict: internal service tokens only; no immediate customer impact detected.

product-security: acknowledging. please keep legal in the loop if tokens map to customer-scoped creds. preliminary hold — no external disclosure yet.

vikram: follow-ups assigned: forensic archive (jordan) -> evidence bucket; network ACL harden (neal); permanent redaction in logging pipeline (sara); legal notification decision (product-security). update timeline in 30m.

sara: also added temporary rule to pipeline to drop any Authorization/Set-Cookie headers before writing logs. will backfill a unit test. :thumbsup:

neal: scan finished: only 3 objects were uploaded to analytics.example.net (timestamps and req ids in evidence). all from hosts with tag staging-logs-5. no prod indicators. uploading CSV to s3://redwood-secure-evidence/incidents/INC-2026-03-17/network_scan.csv

jordan: lowering severity to P2 pending full forensic analysis. still treating as security incident; keeping incident open for timeline and follow-ups.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-03-17 state updated: triage complete, pager cleared. Next update due in 30m.
